history.acceptedBreakingChange: the first snapshot scanned the fixture directory in place, so scan state written by an earlier capture changed the shape (sbomDiff.first); captures now scan a fresh copy each time and are repeatable
fixtures are scanned as one-commit repositories (strict assurance needs history) and a no-history case was added

finding.line is now populated from sink.line (or source.line) for flow-pair and structural findings that carried none, so line-keyed consumers (decorations, git provenance) see a value where the shape used to be optional

the shape merge is canonical: a key optional on both sides is optional once and the result no longer depends on the order of the elements (the old merge serialised nested optionals into text, so the same findings in another order gave a different shape and failed on another host); no public field changed

scanHealth.freshness.epss.ageDays and .stale were always nullable (offline, unavailable, or no CVE to check: number|null and boolean|null, documented in docs/trust/scan-health.md); the 0.195.22 per-scan reset of the feed metadata made the contract scan see the null case instead of a value inherited from an earlier scan in the same process. The documented type is unchanged; the committed shape was

threat-model FR-04.3: findings[].verification.consensus gains independent, conflict, refutationAuthority and groups (additive fields inside an optional object, which the snapshot records as one type string); consensus.verdict is now decided by independent evidence groups instead of lenses, and the per-lens counts keep their meaning

findings[].basis.advisory.affectedRanges, modified and published are no longer recorded: they are null when the advisory feed was unreachable during the scan and populated when it was reachable, so no single recorded type holds on both an offline and an online host (the hosted runner failed the 0.195.28 capture taken offline)
